name: CY8CMBR3116-LQXIT
title: CY8CMBR3xxx CapSense Express capacitive touch controllers: up to 16 buttons, 2 sliders, 2 proximity sensors
summary: Six capacitive touch controllers that run without firmware, five of them configured through an I2C register map: the CY8CMBR3116 (16 sensors, 8 GPOs, 24-pin QFN), CY8CMBR3106S (adds two five-segment sliders), CY8CMBR3110, CY8CMBR3108, CY8CMBR3102 and the hardware-configured CY8CMBR3002. Auto-tuned CSD sensing reads buttons, sliders and proximity electrodes with over 100:1 SNR and drives LEDs, a buzzer, a host interrupt or an analog level, with I2C up to 400 kHz for configuration and status. The supply runs from 1.71 V to 5.5 V; average current is 22 µA per button at a 120 ms refresh.
key_figures: 1.8 V to 5.5 V; 1.71 V to 1.89 V with VCC tied to VDD
22 µA max per button, no touch, 120 ms refresh, EMC off
0.1 pF to 0.4 pF, in four steps
VOL 0.6 V max at 10 mA, 3 V; 85 mA total

notes: Every ordering code also comes on tape and reel, marked by a trailing T (CY8CMBR3116-LQXIT is the CY8CMBR3116-LQXI on tape and reel).

Code fields, left to right: CY (company), 8 (PSoC marketing code), C (CMOS), MBR (mechanical button replacement), 3 (third generation), configuration interface (1 = I2C configurable, 0 = hardware configured), button count (16, 10, 08, 06 or 02), S if sliders are supported, package (LQX = 24- or 16-pin QFN, SX2 = 16-pin SOIC, SX1 = 8-pin SOIC, all Pb-free), I (industrial temperature), then T for tape and reel.
Industrial range: –40 °C to +85 °C.

circuits.title: Four buttons and four LEDs (CY8CMBR3108)
circuits.description: A CY8CMBR3108 reads four touch buttons and lights four LEDs. Each button electrode reaches its CS pin through 560 Ω placed near the chip, for noise immunity. The four GPOs sink LED current: each LED's anode goes through 1 kΩ to VDD and its cathode to the GPO, so the resistor keeps the pin current inside its limit. CMOD takes 2.2 nF and VCC 0.1 µF to ground. VDD and VDDIO (VDDIO no higher than VDD) each get 1 µF and 0.1 µF. SCL and SDA run to the host header through 330 Ω; the bus pull-ups sit on the host side, beyond the header. HI goes to the host to ask it to read the new sensor status.
notes: With VDD from 1.71 V to 1.89 V, VCC is tied to VDD instead of decoupled.
Ground layout matters for SNR.

circuits.title: Proximity sensor, buttons and two sliders (CY8CMBR3106S)
circuits.description: A CY8CMBR3106S with one proximity electrode on PS0, four buttons (CS1 to CS4), a five-segment linear slider on SLD10 to SLD14 and a five-segment radial slider on SLD20 to SLD24. Every sensing line has 560 Ω in series near the chip. Pin 19 drives a one-pin buzzer through 100 Ω; the buzzer's other side returns to VDD. CMOD has 2.2 nF and VCC 0.1 µF to ground; VDD is bypassed with 1 µF and 0.1 µF. SCL and SDA reach the host header through 330 Ω, with the pull-ups on the host side. HI tells the host there is new status to read; XRES is left floating, available as an external reset.
notes: Pin 19 is CS5/SH/HI; in this circuit it drives the buzzer.
Pins 14 to 18 are CS11/SLD20 to CS15/SLD24.
With VDD from 1.71 V to 1.89 V, VCC is shorted to VDD.

circuits.title: Supply connections, 1.8 V ≤ VDD ≤ 5.5 V
circuits.description: Supply wiring for VDD between 1.8 V and 5.5 V, the internal regulator running. VDD carries 0.1 µF and 1 µF to ground, VCC its own 0.1 µF, and VDDIO (1.71 V up to VDD) 1 µF and 0.1 µF.
notes: Only the CY8CMBR3108 has a VDDIO pin; on the other parts the VDDIO connections are absent.

circuits.title: Supply connections, 1.71 V ≤ VDD ≤ 1.89 V
circuits.description: Supply wiring for VDD between 1.71 V and 1.89 V. VCC is tied to VDD, which bypasses the internal regulator; VDD carries 0.1 µF and 1 µF to ground. VDDIO, from 1.71 V up to VDD, gets 1 µF and 0.1 µF. SUPPLY_LOW_POWER in DEVICE_CFG3 must be 1 for operation at 1.8 V ±5%.
notes: Only the CY8CMBR3108 has a VDDIO pin; on the other parts the VDDIO connections are absent.

circuits.title: Analog voltage output from GPOs and a resistor network
circuits.description: Eight buttons each drive their own GPO. Every GPO has a series resistor Rn to one common node, VOUT, which has a single resistor R up to VDD. GPOs are set active low, open drain, sensor-controlled with PWM off: an untouched GPO floats, and a touched one pulls low, so R and that GPO's Rn divide VDD and VOUT reports which button is touched. With FSS enabled only one button reports at a time; if several are touched, their Rn act in parallel.
notes: Applies to a CY8CMBR3xxx with eight GPOs; pin names are the CY8CMBR3116's, on which CSx drives GPOx.

circuits.title: Buzzer connection
circuits.description: A one-input DC piezo buzzer connects from VDDIO to BUZ; the pin's PWM drives it while a touch is being signalled and holds it high otherwise. On a part with no VDDIO pin the buzzer returns to VDD.
notes: Applies to any CY8CMBR3xxx with a buzzer output; the pin name is the CY8CMBR3108's, which has VDDIO.

circuits.title: I2C link to one host
circuits.description: The controller as the only slave on a host's I2C bus. SCL, SDA and the HI interrupt line each have a pull-up resistor to VDD; HI is open drain.
notes: Applies to any CY8CMBR3xxx with I2C and HI; pin names are the CY8CMBR3108's. Pull-up values are not specified.

operation.text: A family of capacitive touch controllers that need no firmware: every feature is set in a register map over I2C (or fixed, on the CY8CMBR3002). Sensing uses the CSD PLUS method with over 100:1 SNR, and SmartSense auto-tuning keeps sensors tuned for PCB, overlay and environment changes at run time.

Up to 16 capacitive sensors per device: up to 16 buttons, up to two five-segment sliders (each linear or radial, or both joined into one ten-segment slider, resolution configurable), and up to two proximity sensors reaching up to 30 cm. Proximity sensors also report touch and accept CP from 8 pF to 45 pF. Sensitivity to 0.1 pF; overlays up to 15 mm of glass or 5 mm of plastic; CP range 5 pF to 45 pF.

Enabling the shield electrode suppresses false touches from water droplets, mist or wet hands; enabling both the shield and the guard sensor also locks out touches under streaming water. Shield and guard each use one pin.

A pseudo-random clock source spreads the sensing clock to cut emissions. An EMC algorithm adds immunity to radiated and conducted noise at the cost of average current, and can be turned off. Buttons and sliders have median and IIR filters; proximity sensors have an advanced low-pass filter.

Sets all button threshold parameters from the measured noise. Applies to buttons only, can be switched off, and is disabled whenever EMC is on. Calculated thresholds can be overridden with register values.

Sets, per button and slider, the minimum capacitance change that changes a sensor's state: 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 or 0.4 pF. Higher sensitivity suits thick overlays or small buttons; lower sensitivity suits large buttons or thin overlays and saves power.

A sensor held active longer than the auto-reset period (5 s or 20 s) is returned to OFF and its baseline reset to the present raw count, so a metal object resting near a sensor cannot leave it stuck. One period applies to all proximity sensors and another to all buttons and slider segments. The guard sensor is never reset.
Enabled per button: when two or more FSS buttons see a touch, only the first touched reports active, so one button at a time is in the touch state.

Up to eight GPOs, shared with sensor inputs. Each follows its sensor or the host over I2C, active low or active high. Drive modes: open drain (high-Z or ground), for LEDs and analog output, or strong (VDD or ground), for logic. PWM with one duty cycle for touch and another for no touch sets LED brightness. A proximity sensor's GPO follows proximity; a touch on it shows only in the register map. GPO state is not kept in Deep Sleep and returns to default on wake. At power-up, faulty sensors are flagged by pulses on their GPOs.
Holds a sensor-driven GPO on for 0 to 2 s, in 20 ms steps, after the touch ends. Set per sensor; not available in toggle mode or when auto reset turned the sensor off.
A sensor-driven GPO changes state on every activation (a touch for a button, an approach for a proximity sensor), like a mechanical toggle switch. Set per sensor; works in every GPO mode.

When a button or guard sensor is touched, the BUZ pin outputs PWM for a buzzer ON time of (1 to 127) × 100 ms, at one of the frequencies in the system table. Repeated touches during the ON time do not restart it. Idle, the pin stays high. Buzzer output and EMC must not both be enabled.

Any change in sensor status or slider position sends an active-low pulse of width THI on the HI pin, which is open drain; pulses are at least one refresh interval apart. Only one pin can be HI on parts that offer it on several. On the CY8CMBR3108, HI runs from VDDIO so it can talk to a host at a lower voltage than VDD.
Current status (BUTTON_STAT) and latched status (LATCHED_BUTTON_STAT) can both be read, so a touch that ended before the host read it is not lost.

At every reset a built-in test checks sensors, shield and CMOD. A failing sensor is disabled and its GPO gets a 50 ms pulse; a failing shield or CMOD disables all sensors and pulses all GPOs. Pulses come during boot, and results are also in the register map. A sensor with CP over 45 pF is disabled; CMOD below 1 nF or above 4 nF disables all sensors. Shorts detected: sensor to VSS (except on the pin that is also AXRES), to VDD, to another sensor, and to shield.
If power fails while a configuration is being saved, the next reset loads the last valid configuration, or the factory default if the user never saved one.

VDD is the main supply: 1.8 V to 5.5 V with the internal regulator, or 1.8 V ±5% with it bypassed. All I/O except I2C, HI and XRES is referred to VDD. VDDIO, on the parts that have it, supplies I2C SDA, SCL, HI and XRES, from 1.71 V up to VDD, never above VDD; without VDDIO those pins are referred to VDD. VCC is the regulator output feeding the core and sensing circuits; it needs a 0.1 µF, 5 V ceramic capacitor close to the pin. VDD and VDDIO need no sequencing. VSS and the exposed pad both go to board ground.

Parts leave the factory set for 1.8 V to 5.5 V. For 1.8 V ±5% operation: short VCC to VDD, power at 1.8 V (configuration works at 1.8 V whatever the bit; only sensing is not guaranteed until it is set), set SUPPLY_LOW_POWER in DEVICE_CFG3 to 1 (EZ-Click does this automatically), save and reset. With VCC shorted to VDD, VDD must stay at or below 1.89 V.

Boot loads the last configuration and runs diagnostics. Active scans every 20 ms (or the scan and processing time, if longer) and drives outputs. With no touch for the STATE_TIMEOUT time, the device drops to Look-for-Touch, scanning all sensors at the slower REFRESH_CTRL interval and driving only PWM or toggle GPOs. With wake-on-approach on and toggle off, it next drops to Look-for-Proximity, scanning only the wake-on-approach proximity sensors and driving nothing; a detected approach returns it to Look-for-Touch and a touch to Active. Deep Sleep, entered and left on host command (an I2C address match wakes it), scans nothing and resets GPOs to default. A configuration change, or a corrupt configuration found at boot, puts it in Configuration, waiting for reset.
In each refresh interval the device sleeps after scanning. Any I2C traffic, or SCL held low, keeps it awake to avoid NACKs, so for lowest current the bus must be idle with SCL and SDA pulled up.

Response times are estimated with the design toolbox: first button touch while in either low-rate scanning state (RFBT), consecutive button touches in Active (RCBT), first and consecutive slider touches (RFST, RCST), button and slider release (RBSR), proximity detect (RProx) and proximity release (RProx_release).
Three equivalent resets, each ending in Boot: cycling VDD, holding XRES low for at least TXRES, and writing the SW_RESET command.

I2C slave up to 400 kHz with a configurable 7-bit address from 0x08 to 0x77 (I2C_ADDR register; default 0x37). Repeated START is supported; the device never stretches the clock or stalls the bus. Single-slave and multi-slave buses both work.

Wait TI2CBOOT after reset before talking; earlier attempts are NACKed. A device in its low-power state NACKs its address, wakes, and keeps NACKing until it is Active, so the host retries until ACK. A gap of more than 340 ms between bytes in one transaction can let the device sleep and NACK. After SAVE_CHECK_CRC (220 ms typ), all transactions are NACKed until it finishes. Writes to read-only registers are ignored.

Write: START, address with write bit (retry with repeated START until ACK), register address, then data bytes that fill successive registers, then STOP. Setting the read pointer: the same up to the register address, then STOP. Read: START, address with write bit, repeated START with the address until ACK, then the device returns bytes from successive registers, the host ACKing each and NACKing the last, then STOP.
